title: Elorian’s first AI model wants to reason with images, not just about them
key_facts: Elorian, a Palo Alto AI start-up that raised a $55 million seed round at a $300 million valuation before launching a product, released its first model, Glimpse, on Friday 16 Oct 2026, as a research preview with API access and a chat interface (TechCrunch exclusive).

Most multimodal models look at an image once, convert it to tokens and reason in text; Glimpse goes back to the source mid-reasoning, cropping into a region, pulling video frames or running code to measure, which Elorian calls a 'visual scratch space'.
The approach is not completely new: OpenAI added crop-and-zoom during reasoning to its o-series models in 2025.
Elorian says a small team trained Glimpse on a few hundred GPUs and the model is substantially smaller than the frontier systems it is compared with.
Price: $0.60 per million tokens in and $3 per million out, cheaper than mid-level models such as Sonnet and Sol, more expensive than lightweight ones such as Haiku and Luna.
By Elorian's evaluations Glimpse beats GPT-6 Astra on scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning, with competitive results on other visual reasoning tasks.

Andrew Dai, Elorian's CEO and a former Google DeepMind researcher, says AI models still cannot really see; investors include Striker Venture Partners, Menlo Ventures, Altimeter Capital, Nvidia and Jeff Dean, Google's chief scientist.

why_it_matters_hint: A new start-up bets that models which re-inspect images while reasoning can beat bigger systems on visual tasks at lower cost, though the results are its own.
